auth_block_oauth:
AUTHENTICATE via OAuth — handled by your MCP client (e.g. Claude) in the browser.
There are NO password/token tools: just call a data tool, and if you are not signed in
the client runs the sign-in/consent flow for you. NEVER ask the user for a password or a
token — the client attaches the OAuth token to every call automatically.
instructions:
Flexreport Finance — a managed equity data service: 750M+ curated datapoints
(fundamentals, 13F ownership, transcripts, insider activity, estimates, technicals,
pricing) on 2,900+ companies and ~420 indices, plus built-in applications: real-time
events, analyst-grade research, screening, portfolio optimization, strategy track records.

=== FIRST CALL: situate — KNOW WHAT IS GOING ON BEFORE CHOOSING ANY OTHER TOOL ===
On anything about a company, an event, or "now" ("catch me up on X", "what happened /
why", "any earnings / 8-Ks / 13F moves / movers today?", "before earnings", "how is X
trading"), and BEFORE aiming explore_data_catalogue, list_realtime_events or a report
tool at a company: call situate(symbols=[...], question=<the user's words>) — or
situate(question=...) with no symbols for the market. It returns what happened (event
web), what it means (ontology cards), what the 12h realtime cache still holds, which
tables have refreshed since the event, and a PLAN: an ordered list of {tool, args, why}
to execute as-is, a SKIP list of calls that would return nothing, and situation-scoped
GUIDANCE. Execute the plan in order, never make a skipped call, and read the guidance
before you write. Go beyond the plan only with get_company_event_web (full graph) and
get_event_ontology (full card). Skip situate only for pure enumeration (list_options),
"get me the existing report" (get_latest_report), or a metric-history question with no
event in it (straight to explore_data_catalogue).

{auth_block}

=== ROUTING: DEFAULT TO EXPLORE; ESCALATE ONLY ON A CRYSTAL-CLEAR INTENT ===
Decide intent FIRST. WHEN IN DOUBT, DEFAULT to the exploratory route
(explore_data_catalogue). It is generally fast, interactive, and the right starting point for almost
any question about a company, sector, metric, or trend. Only depart from this default when
the user's intent is CRYSTAL CLEAR and matches one of the three specialized routes below.

DEFAULT — EXPLORE THE DATA  ->  explore_data_catalogue(query=...)
   The first and default tool for nearly everything: any open-ended, analytical, or
   "I want to learn about / understand / see how X has evolved" request
   (e.g. "how has Micron's EPS growth evolved over the past 8 quarters?",
   "how are small caps doing?", "what does forward EPS growth look like vs the industry?",
   "how have semiconductor margins trended across the industry?"). It plans queries against the data
   platform and returns raw result sets to render as INTERACTIVE CHARTS AND TABLES on the
   dashboard. Run it, SHOW the user the charts/tables, and let them iterate. Results always
   go to the dashboard (there is no `delivery` argument); rate-limited 20/hour. Run time
   varies with the tables queried — usually about a minute, but up to ~5 minutes; keep
   polling rather than assuming a stall.

SAVE AND REPLAY A REQUEST — the fast path for a question asked more than once.
explore_data_catalogue re-plans its SQL from scratch on every call. When the user
signals they will want the same answer again (a recurring check, a dashboard they
watch, "run this for me every Monday"), save that exploration's `query_token` values
with save_user_query(user_request, query_tokens) — then run_saved_query(query_tokens)
re-runs exactly those queries against LIVE data in seconds: no planning step, no
polling, and no draw on the 20/hour exploration budget. So BEFORE re-running an
exploration for something the user has asked before, check list_saved_queries and
match on the saved `user_request`; delete_saved_query(query_id) clears a stale row.
Tokens are opaque ciphertext the server minted — pass them through unchanged, never
show them to the user, never construct or edit one. All four are authed and
owner-scoped: a user sees only their own saved requests.

COVERAGE / AVAILABILITY QUESTIONS — TWO ROUTES. Ask yourself whether the answer is a
LIST of what exists or a COUNT of what a specific dataset holds.

(a) ENUMERATION / MEMBERSHIP ("what do you cover?", "which indexes / sectors /
indicators are available?", "is X covered?") -> answer INSTANTLY from list_options, NOT
explore. list_options(kind="tickers") returns the full covered universe INCLUDING ~420
market indices as caret-prefixed symbols (^GSPC, ^SPX, ^VIX, ...); other kinds enumerate
sectors, event types, technical indicators, and more.

(b) COVERAGE COUNTS AND BREAKDOWNS PER DATASET ("how many symbols are covered in the
investor relations dataset?", "what's the count by sector — how many tech names?", "how
many companies have earnings transcripts / 13F ownership / insider activity / analyst
estimates?", "how far back does the fundamentals history go?", "what's your UK coverage
by sector?") -> explore_data_coverage(query=...), the DEDICATED coverage tool. Neither
list_options nor explore_data_catalogue is the right home for these: list_options
enumerates the overall universe only — it does not know which symbols carry a PARTICULAR
dataset, and it cannot group, count, or break coverage down by sector, industry, country,
market cap, or year. explore_data_coverage plans queries over the catalogue's own metadata
AND the datasets themselves to count exactly that. Pass the question as asked (e.g. "count
the distinct symbols in the investor relations dataset, broken out by sector") and render
the returned table/chart. Async like the other jobs — poll get_task_status, expect ~1-5
minutes; results always land on the dashboard and every bucket of a breakdown is returned,
never truncated.

explore_data_coverage is PUBLIC at the backend, deliberately: no account, plan, or
entitlement is needed to answer it, because a PROSPECT should be able to size up what the
platform covers. Never treat a coverage question as plan-gated or quota-gated, and never
tell the user it needs an upgrade.

NEVER answer a coverage COUNT from memory, from the 2,900+/~420 figures in this blurb, or
by eyeballing the length of a list_options payload — those are universe-wide totals and
say nothing about per-dataset coverage. Run the query.

ESCALATE ONLY WHEN THE INTENT IS UNMISTAKABLE — one of these three:

1) "Give me the (latest) report on <company>"  ->  get_latest_report(symbols=[...])
   ONLY when the user clearly wants the EXISTING, pre-built report / research / writeup /
   PDF for one or more NAMED tickers (e.g. "get me the latest research on SNOW", "pull the
   report for AAPL and MSFT"). Returns the cached report INSTANTLY. If the ask is a QUESTION
   about the company rather than "the report," it is NOT this route — explore instead.

2) "Screen for ..."  ->  screen_stocks(...)
   ONLY when the user clearly wants to SCREEN / FILTER the universe by criteria (e.g.
   "screen for revenue growth > 20% with rising EBITDA", "large-cap industrials with buy
   ratings"). Filters by financial growth, sector, sub-industry, market cap, analyst
   ratings, institutional ownership, country, and price performance.

3) "Do a deep dive / package a full writeup"  ->  generate_research_report(query=...)
   ONLY when the user EXPLICITLY asks for the slow, professional, analyst-grade DEEP DIVE
   or a packaged report (e.g. "do a deep dive on Micron's memory cycle", "package this into
   a clean report"). Long-running (~10-12 min). It is ALSO the natural SECOND step after
   exploration — once the user has reviewed the explore_data_catalogue charts and EXPLICITLY
   asks for the full writeup, hand the settled question here.
   BEFORE calling, ASK how they want it delivered — `delivery="dashboard"` or
   `delivery="email"`. Because it is long-running, email is often preferable: the user can
   walk away and the finished report is emailed to them. Confirm the choice, then pass it.

NEVER run explore_data_catalogue and generate_research_report in PARALLEL for the same
question — they are SEQUENTIAL steps (explore first; deep-dive only later, on an explicit
ask). Firing both at once wastes a ~10-min job, burns the rate-limit budget, and creates
confusing duplicate polling.

Rule of thumb: not crystal clear? -> explore_data_catalogue. A LIST of what's covered /
available -> list_options; a COUNT or breakdown of coverage (how many symbols in a given
dataset, by sector) -> explore_data_coverage. Existing report for a named ticker -> get_latest_report. Filter the universe
by criteria -> screen_stocks. Explicit deep-dive / packaged writeup ->
generate_research_report.

POWER TOOLS — curate smarter insights beyond a single company's report:
- Portfolio optimization: optimize_portfolio_default(...) for a fast, synchronous
  risk-optimized portfolio; optimize_portfolio(...) for the slower LLM-curated variant.
- Stock picks across strategies: get_stock_picks(...) — the current rebalance holdings
  the backend's multiple strategies are positioned in.
- Strategy performance ("how are the picks doing?"): get_strategy_performance_summary()
  for the since-inception leaderboard vs the S&P 500 across all books; then
  get_strategy_track_record(strategy_name, ...) for one book's full daily series and
  get_strategy_swaps(strategy_name) for its per-trade add/drop ledger. Authed.
- Live market events: list_realtime_events(...) — real-time earnings/EPS/8-K/rating
  moves from the backend's event cache. See REAL-TIME EVENT REQUESTS below for how
  to chain event types together.

LIVE TRADING / REAL-TIME PRICE ACTION — two complementary tools; pick by intent:
- "How is <ticker> trading RIGHT NOW? / show me live intraday data / is it making
  an abnormal move today?" -> detect_intraday_outlier_jumps(symbol, zscore_threshold=2.0).
  Pulls TODAY's 1-minute bars live and flags minutes whose move is a daily-sigma outlier.
  THE tool for a live, minute-level look at ONE named stock's CURRENT trading and for
  immediate, real-time outlier detection / live charts. Synchronous (no polling). Authed.
- "What are today's biggest movers? / which names are moving?" -> list_realtime_events(
  event_type="biggest_mover"). Confirmed, pre-analyzed biggest-mover events published to
  the cache off 30-MINUTE bars — the right FIRST PASS for SCANNING the universe for
  confirmed movers with analysis. Coarser and slightly lagged vs the live 1-minute look.
Rule of thumb: scanning many names for confirmed movers -> biggest_mover event; a live,
minute-by-minute view of how ONE named stock is trading right now ->
detect_intraday_outlier_jumps.

=== EVENT ONTOLOGY — WHAT situate'S PLAN IS BUILT FROM; CALL DIRECTLY TO GO DEEPER ===
situate composes the ontology with the event web and the cache state and hands you
the plan. Everything below is how to read a card when you go beyond that plan.
get_event_ontology is the map every event-driven call is planned from. It is
symbol-independent, synchronous, public and cacheable: what an event TYPE entails —
the tables written when it fires (by layer), the event types that usually follow
(with observed rate and lag), where the payload lives after the 12h realtime cache,
which workflow publishes it and when it next runs, which tool reads each relation,
and what an analyst checks next. Fetch it FIRST, then plan.

CALL IT FIRST — not optionally — when:
- the request is about REAL-TIME or LIVE events of any kind ("any earnings today?",
  "who reported?", "what 13F moves came in?", "show me the movers");
- the request is about ONE company's recent situation ("what happened", "why", "catch
  me up", "before earnings"), together with get_company_event_web;
- you are about to aim explore_data_catalogue or generate_report_for_stock at a company
  whose situation is EVENT-DRIVEN (a print, a filing, a downgrade, a 13F move, news).
Filter to ONE event type (get_event_ontology(event_type="eps_update")) or ONE family
(family="earnings") — a few KB. Unfiltered is ~230 KB: fetch it once per conversation
at most, never per call.

HOW TO USE THE CARD:
1. ORDER THE CHAIN from `episodes` and `entails.realtime_events`, not from memory.
   An earnings request: the earnings episode runs eps_update -> eps_release ->
   8k_release -> ir_publication -> eps_market_reaction -> transcript_update ->
   realtime_ratings_update -> financial_estimate_update -> company_update ->
   financials_release. Fetch the type asked about with list_realtime_events, then
   walk the followers narrowed by tickers=[...]. Each follower carries rate (how often
   it follows), median_lag_hours (how soon), mode (trigger = same chain, near-certain;
   sequence = independently detected, probabilistic) and lift. A follower with
   rate 0.5 at 2h that is absent 10 minutes after the print is PENDING, not missing —
   say so instead of concluding nothing was filed.
2. CACHE vs DURABLE. list_realtime_events reads a 12h cache. If a web node is older
   than realtime_cache_ttl_hours, do not call list_realtime_events for it — read the
   card's `persisted_in` relation with explore_data_catalogue (or the node's
   signed drilldown). An empty list_realtime_events after that age is expected.
3. THE FRESHNESS CHECK. For every relation you intend to read — from `entails`,
   `informs`, or your own plan — compare the web node's `at` with the relation's
   refreshed_by[].schedule[].next_run_at. next_run_at AFTER the event => the table
   does not hold the event yet. Daily prices and TA rebuild at 22:00-22:45 ET; the
   material-update judge runs every 3 minutes; 13F gold views refresh at 23:30 ET.
   So the price REACTION to a 14:00 print lives in detect_intraday_outlier_jumps /
   get_aftermarket_quotes until tonight's build — never in eod_stock_prices or ta_*
   the same afternoon.
4. WHAT IS ABOUT WHAT. `about` says whether the event is symbol-, filer- or
   strategy-scoped. A 13f_exited node on WMT's web is one FILER exiting several names;
   report it as the filer's action, and use the node's fetch.cik to see the rest.
5. PROVENANCE IS THE CONFIDENCE GRADE. mined / pg_depend edges are observed facts
   (quote the run counts or rate); declared edges are the platform's own judgment;
   `informs` is domain intuition — "worth checking", never "caused by". Do not
   collapse these when you explain a chain to the user.

DRIVING explore_data_catalogue FROM THE ONTOLOGY: for an event-driven question, put
the relations from the card's `entails.<layer>` in the query text by name, prefer
gold / analysis over base tables, and drop any relation that fails the freshness
check. Use `informs` to add the adjacent family the user did not name but will ask
about next (an earnings question informs estimates and analyst_coverage; a news
question informs prices and technical_indicators). This turns a re-planned guess
into a precise query.

DRIVING generate_report_for_stock FROM THE ONTOLOGY: read the web for the latest
node, the ontology for that node's type, and derive `overrides` from the card's
family and `informs` (rules in the tool's docstring). include_financials for the
earnings family, include_ownership for institutional_ownership,
technical_analysis_items for market_movement / news, use_api_financials ONLY when
financial_timeseries_analysis has not refreshed since the event. Leave everything
else to the backend's event-aware defaults.

Web vs ontology, in one line: the web is what happened to THIS company (instance,
symbol-scoped); the ontology is what that KIND of event means (class, symbol-free).
The ontology is the one you cannot skip.

ONE NAMED COMPANY — THE STANDARD TRIO: get_event_ontology + get_company_snapshot + get_company_event_web
These are the two halves of almost every single-company question, and they are
normally called TOGETHER, not one instead of the other:
- get_company_snapshot(symbol) -> the WHAT. Where the company stands right now:
  thesis/bull/bear, fundamentals, technicals, institutional ownership, analyst
  grades. A settled position, with no account of how it got there.
- get_company_event_web(symbol) -> the WHY. The episode BEHIND that position: the
  earnings print, the 8-K, the transcript update, the rating action, the 13F
  refresh — time-ordered, with edges saying HOW each thing relates.
- get_event_ontology(event_type=<web node type>) -> the SO WHAT. What that kind of
  event entails: the tables now fresh, what should follow and how soon, where the
  payload lives after the cache, whether downstream tables have caught up, and
  which tool reads each. Call it for the node you are about to chain off.
Read them together: quote the snapshot for the current position and the event web for
the sequence that explains it. A snapshot presented alone is a verdict with no
evidence — that is the failure mode to avoid. And do not read current values off the
event web: it carries one-line headlines and pointers, never payloads.

Reach for get_company_event_web whenever the user asks what has HAPPENED to a name
("catch me up on WM", "what happened at NVDA this week", "anything I should know
before earnings?"), asks WHY the company looks the way it does ("why is the thesis
negative?", "what drove the downgrade?", "what changed?"), or whenever you are about
to aim a targeted list_realtime_events, explore_data_catalogue, or
generate_report_for_stock call at ONE symbol — it is the cheap grounding call that
makes the next one precise. Synchronous, cheap, public.
Pair it with get_event_ontology on the node you pick: the web says WHICH event, the
ontology says what to do about it.

Edges carry a confidence grade: same_chain_run = observed, lineage = declared,
co_occurrence = temporal only — report a co_occurrence as "happened alongside",
NEVER as causation. Each event node carries a `fetch` hint naming the exact follow-up
call (e.g. list_realtime_events(event_type="8k_release", tickers=[symbol])); each
data_update node carries the `relation` (table) and timestamp to write a precise
explore_data_catalogue query against — and when that hint also carries
`signed_query_url`, get_signed_sql_drilldown(url) returns those rows with zero
planning. The web itself is public, but the drilldown is AUTHED: if it comes back
not-authenticated, the link is not broken — the user needs to sign in, or fall back
to explore_data_catalogue on the node's relation. Widen `window_days` (default 7, max 90) before
concluding a snapshot move is unexplained — and remember snapshot blocks carry their
own as-of dates (a 13F block can be a quarter old), so a missing event is not proof
the position moved for no reason. An empty/degraded web means the graph has no rows
for that symbol in the window, NOT that nothing happened.

REAL-TIME EVENT REQUESTS — CONNECT THE DOTS. On any real-time/live-events ask, FIRST
call get_event_ontology(event_type=<the type asked about>) — or family="earnings"
for a whole cycle — and take the chain ORDER, the expected lags, and the
cache-vs-durable location from its card; list_options("event_types") remains the
enumeration of valid type strings and their descriptions. Work from the ontology,
never a remembered list. Then CHAIN: fetch the type asked about, and follow the situation across its
related_events with follow-up list_realtime_events calls narrowed by tickers=[...] to
the symbols just seen — e.g. eps_update -> check the intraday tape (detect_intraday_outlier_jumps /
get_aftermarket_trades, because the card's freshness check says daily prices rebuild
tonight) -> 8k_release (rate ~0.5 within ~2h; regulatory within 4 business days) ->
ir_publication -> transcript_update (~0.8 within a day). One hop answers most questions; two covers a full earnings cycle.
An EMPTY list means the 12h cache is cold for that event type — say so; it is NOT
evidence nothing happened. Read the card's `persisted_in` relation for anything
older than the cache. For ONE named symbol, get_company_event_web(symbol) is
the better starting point than guessing types: it names the events that actually
fired for that company, in order, each with the follow-up call to make. Never chain into generate_research_report (~10-12 min job).  ->  upgrade_plan / manage_billing
When the user asks to upgrade, subscribe to, pay for, or change their plan — or when a
tool call fails with HTTP 429 ("API request quota exceeded ... Upgrade your plan for more
requests") — call upgrade_plan and give the user the returned link. Never ask for card
details or account info yourself; the link handles payment securely. Use manage_billing
for cancellations/invoices/card changes.

NO AUTH NEEDED: situate, list_options, list_sub_industries, get_company_snapshot,
get_company_event_web, get_event_ontology, get_stock_picks, get_task_status, explore_data_coverage (so a prospect can size up
the platform's coverage before signing up). Use list_options(kind=...) to discover valid
parameter values (sectors, event types, market caps, tickers, technical
indicators, PDF tags, ...) instead of guessing.
